_comment: Narration for 'How a stealth bomber avoids radar'. '|' marks where a subtitle chunk ends (it is not spoken). 'gap' = seconds of silence before the line. 'scene' = which visual scene starts with this line.

lines.text: This bomber is | a hundred and seventy-two feet wide. | Yet on radar, | it can look | about as small | as a bird.
Radar sends out | radio waves | and listens for the echo. | Stealth means | sending back | as little echo | as possible.
One: | the flying wing. | No tail fins, | no bulky fuselage. | Just one smooth, | blended shape | with fewer corners | to catch a signal.
Two: | its edges are lined up | at just a few angles, | so radar waves | glance off | and scatter away | from the receiver.
Three: | radar-absorbent coatings | turn part of | the incoming energy | into heat, | weakening the echo.
Four: | the engines are buried | inside the wing. | Hot exhaust | mixes with cool air | and exits over the top, | shielded from sensors below.
Five: | weapons ride | inside internal bays. | Bombs hanging | under the wing | would add | extra echoes.
Together, | the echo shrinks | dramatically. | It's not invisible. | But it gets detected | much later, | and much closer.
The twist? | Shrink an echo | ten thousand times, | and detection range | only drops | about ten times. | What should I | break down next?
